System

Levels, derived stats and profession progression

Character XP/levels and profession skill are separate durable tracks. The level cap is data-defined; derived combat attributes are rebuilt from class growth, level, equipment, talents and valid effects rather than saved as competing authoritative totals.

Scope and player interaction

Character XP/levels and profession skill are separate durable tracks. The level cap is data-defined; derived combat attributes are rebuilt from class growth, level, equipment, talents and valid effects rather than saved as competing authoritative totals.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase08committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

CurrentLevel → XPPending → LeveledUp → AtCap → RebuildPending

WBP_Stats observes results from URPGProgressionComponent. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: DA_Progression_Default. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
CharacterXP: cumulative nonnegative bigint; no float XP
LevelCap=50; strictly increasing authored cumulative thresholds
Level: derived from XP and threshold table, persisted only as validated cache if needed
SkillPointsEarned/Spent: derived/recorded under talent rules; cannot become negative
ProfessionXP: map by profession definition ID; independent thresholds
DerivedStatInputs: class, level, equipped item revisions, purchased talents; no UI-owned values

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGProgressionComponentImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_StatsLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
ApplyXPReceipt(RewardReceipt) -> Updated|AlreadyApplied; committed backend result
ResolveLevel(CumulativeXP, CurveVersion) -> Level; deterministic pure rule
RebuildDerivedStats(BuildSnapshot) -> ValidatedAttributes|InvalidBuild; server
ApplyProfessionXP(ProfessionId, VerifiedCommand) -> Updated|Rejected; part of gather/craft/fish transaction

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. A verified defeat/quest/gather/craft/fish command produces a durable XP delta under its domain rule, never from a UI animation.
  2. Backend applies delta once and validates the threshold-table version; level changes and earned skill-point changes are returned in the same result.
  3. Zone updates progression cache and rebuilds derived attribute inputs through the one GAS initialization/modifier path.
  4. Health/max-resource changes follow an explicit policy: preserve current percentage on a max-stat rebuild while clamping bounds; do not fully heal on equipment swap.
  5. Owner UI displays XP/level and a level-up cue keyed to receipt/revision; remote nameplates see only public level.
  6. At cap, stop character XP progression under the chosen cap policy while allowing professions/quests/items to remain useful; no impossible prerequisite beyond cap.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. Author DT_LevelThresholds with rows 1..50 and strictly increasing cumulative XP. Start with a small test threshold so Slice B can prove leveling, then restore catalog values.
  2. Create DA_Progression_Default linking class growth and threshold data. Do not hardcode level 50 in widgets.
  3. Add URPGProgressionComponent to PlayerState after native compilation; it owns in-zone read-only projections of durable progression.
  4. Bind WBP_Stats and HUD XP display to progression delegates, and enemy/quest reward owners to the backend receipt pathway.
  5. Reopen equipment/talent/GAS consumers to call RebuildDerivedStats after committed build revisions; do not stack a second permanent effect on every refresh.

Reopen Phase08 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: L_Rillmere / Character_A / XPGrantFixture. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
Replay XP receipt -> unchanged cumulative XP.
Threshold table contains duplicate/decreasing row -> content validator fails before admission.
Equip/unequip repeatedly -> identical final stats, no accumulated hidden bonuses.
At level 50 receive XP -> declared cap result, no level 51 or negative bar.
Profession reward after reconnect -> one profession increment tied to original gather/craft/fish command.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

Suggested early tuning curve: XP needed for next level = 100 + 30*(level-1)^2; use a Data Table and playtest pacing. This is not a balanced 50-level campaign.

Log XP source entitlement and input build revision. Stats tooltip separates base, level, equipment, talent and temporary modifiers; do not reveal hidden server anti-abuse values.

Art gaps, production and do-not-build-yet

The asset ZIP and installed PaperZD APIs remain unverified. Required new art/unsupported layer combinations are tracked in art/animation-matrix.html and art/equipment-visual-matrix.html. A legal debug visual can prove authority but is not finished content. Production features listed as later/optional remain disabled until their phase/gate passes.
